citations.assessment: The Bavli calls Rav Meri a son of Rav Kahana in the egg case.
The printed patronymic matches in the discussion of impurity and ḥallah.
The dog-and-door inference is attributed to Rav Meri son of Rav Kahana.
The printed named patronymic matches in the stones or projectile liability discussion.
Meri with this patronymic in the ox and plowing locus.
Rav Meri son of Rav Kahana teaches the verse interpretation.
The pinned reference lacks a folio side. The cited Mari occurrence is on 12a, in the redemption argument.
The bloodletting discussion attributes the hide/meat explanation to Rav Meri son of Rav Kahana.

holds.raw: והשארית יוסף מנאו בתלמידי רב ולא ידעתי מנ"ל
holds.reason: Target witnesses are Mantua 1593, 36a (Fordham/Internet Archive sefersheerityose008800) and Warsaw 1909, p. 72 (HebrewBooks 35049, viewer p. 77). The printed lines were not directly checked during this batch. The studenthood inference remains contested.

holds.raw: דהא רב כהנא אביו היה תלמיד רב
holds.reason: The cited Rav Meri occurrences support the patronymic. Which Rav Kahana this is and the cross-generational studenthood implication require distinct evidence.
